Subject: Dedicated pool behavior & carveout ask for Nov peak

Aisha / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated offering looks promising. We are working through internal procurement and infra approvals for a reserved GPU commitment that would cover our Black Friday workload. Before the execs greenlight the spend we need clarity on how Redwood will treat:

- in-flight requests during short maintenance events (we have many short-lived spikes)
- queueing behavior when our reserved pool is saturated (what gets throttled vs prioritized)
- guaranteed minimum throughput during multi-region failovers

We have a couple of concrete asks: a written carveout that guarantees minimum sustained throughput for our reserved pool during a 4-hour Black Friday window, and a documented inflight/queueing behavior section we can attach to the SOW.

I attached an outline (atlas-sla-request-outline.pdf) and a short token forecast (token-usage-forecast.csv) so you can see our shape. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a headroom carveout or an SLO exception for the peak window, and what the technical controls would be?

If easier, happy to do a brief call. Looking to close procurement by mid-June.

—Tom

Aisha / team — looping in some technical detail that can be used directly in the SOW addendum. Attaching a short tech note (will paste key bits below) and I can export a one-page PDF if needed.

--- quoted text from Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@atlaslogistics.com> ---
> We have a couple of concrete asks: a written carveout that guarantees minimum sustained throughput for our reserved pool during a 4-hour Black Friday window, and a documented inflight/queueing behavior section we can attach to the SOW.

Summary (engineer view):
1) Reserved pool minimum sustained throughput
   - We can expose a contractual "sustained token throughput" floor expressed as tokens/sec per reserved GPU equivalence. Practically we guarantee a throughput floor for the reserved pool (not per customer-wide shared pools) for the specified time window. For Atlas-sized commitments we expect to guarantee ~70–80% of the pool's theoretical throughput during high contention windows if standard autoscaling is disabled for the pool. Exact numbers will depend on model family and seq length — we recommend specifying the model tag and P95 sequence length in the SOW.

2) Inflight request handling / queueing behavior
   - Short requests (<3s inference) are served with priority weighting for reserved-pool tokens; longer KV-warmup requests are queued into a tail queue with separate concurrency limits to avoid head-of-line blocking. We use continuous batching but maintain per-customer priority buckets. During saturation, reserved-pool traffic is allowed to preempt best-effort workloads within the same physical pool; preemption is by request chunk, not by process kill, to preserve serving correctness.

3) Failover and multi-region considerations
   - For multi-region failover we can provision a cold standby pool (capacity reserved but powered down) that can be pre-warmed within a configured warmup window (30–90 minutes). A contractual guarantee can reference a warmup SLA: e.g., 80% throughput restored within 60 minutes of failover initiation. Note: immediate (sub-minute) full-throughput guarantees are not feasible without always-on hot standby, which materially increases cost.

4) Operational controls and observability
   - We will expose per-route token/sec metrics, queue-depth, and per-request priority tags in the Console. For the SOW we can include a requirement that Redwood provides a dedicated alerting playbook and a runbook handoff during the Black Friday window.

5) Proposed mitigations for headroom shortfalls
   - Reserved burst credits: small pool of burst capacity that can be consumed during the 4-hour window, replenished monthly.
   - Graceful degradation policy: degrade non-essential reranking steps first, keep inference pipeline endpoints that serve customer-facing scoring at higher priority.

Attachments: I will export a 1-page tech note and two example metric graphs (token-rate vs latency) to illustrate expected behavior.

If you want numbers to drop into the SOW: tell me which model (we'll assume LLM-v2-small quantized) and the P95 sequence length and I'll produce an estimated tokens/sec per GPU equivalence and a conservative floor for the window.

—Dev
Dev Patel

- We need the 4-hour window to be region-local (US-East primary) but willing to accept a 60-minute warmup if we must rely on a cold standby in a secondary region.
